## Summary

The repo is at `/workspace/repo`. The key files are `src/AggregateFunctions/SingleValueData.h`, `src/AggregateFunctions/SingleValueData.cpp`, and `src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionSingleValueOrNull.cpp`.

### 1. Which variant handles complex types like JSON

`SingleValueData.h` defines a `SingleValueDataBase` virtual base with specializations:
- `SingleValueDataFixed<T>` / `SingleValueDataNumeric<T>` — numeric types
- `SingleValueDataString` — String
- `SingleValueDataGeneric` — "any other value type", stores a `Field`
- `SingleValueDataGenericWithColumn` — same role but stores the value inside an `IColumn` (`ColumnPtr`) instead of a `Field`

The dispatch (both `createAggregateFunctionSingleValue`, header lines 440-442, and `generateSingleValueFromType`, `.cpp` lines 1653-1663) decides between the two generic variants using `canUseFieldForValueData` (`.cpp` line 1601):

```cpp
bool canUseFieldForValueData(const DataTypePtr & value_type)
{
    bool result = true;
    auto check = [&](const IDataType & type)
    {
        /// Variant, Dynamic and Object types doesn't work well with Field
        /// because they can store values of different data types in a single column.
        result &= !isVariant(type) && !isDynamic(type) && !isObject(type);
    };
    check(*value_type);
    value_type->forEachChild(check);
    return result;
}
```

So **JSON (the `Object` type) is deliberately routed to `SingleValueDataGenericWithColumn`, not `SingleValueDataGeneric`** — because JSON does not round-trip cleanly through `Field`.

### 2. `SingleValueDataGeneric` (Field-based) — full code

Declaration (`SingleValueData.h:320-345`): private `Field value;`, `has()` returns `!value.isNull()`.

Implementation (`SingleValueData.cpp:1301-1408`): `set` uses `column.get(row_num, value)`; `insertResultInto` uses `to.insert(value)`; `write`/`read` use `serialization.serializeBinary(value, buf, {})` / `deserializeBinary(value, buf, {})`; `isEqualTo` compares `value == column[row_num]`; `setIfSmaller`/`setIfGreater` pull a `Field new_value` via `column.get` and compare with `<`/`>`. (Pasted in full during investigation.)

The relevant `SingleValueDataGenericWithColumn` path used for JSON (`SingleValueData.cpp:1412-1523`) stores a `ColumnPtr value`; `set` clones the argument column and does `insertFrom` + `removeSpecialRepresentations`; comparisons use `ColumnObject::compareAt`; `write` serializes `*value` at row 0; and critically `read` (line 1431) does:

```cpp
void SingleValueDataGenericWithColumn::read(ReadBuffer & buf, const ISerialization & serialization, const DataTypePtr & type, Arena *)
{
    ...
    auto new_value = type->createColumn();   // <-- builds column from the passed type
    new_value->reserve(1);
    serialization.deserializeBinary(*new_value, buf, {});
    value = std::move(new_value);
}
```

### 3. JSON and `Field`

JSON does technically support `Field` round-tripping: `ColumnObject::operator[]`/`get` (`src/Columns/ColumnObject.cpp:236-270`) build an `Object` `Field` (a `std::map` of path → sub-Field), and `ColumnObject::insert(const Field&)` (line 471) / `tryInsert` reconstruct from an `Object` field. But this is lossy: the code comments note it "cannot distinguish cases when dynamic path has Null value and when it's absent in the row," and dynamic-path type information is not preserved. That is exactly why `canUseFieldForValueData` excludes `Object`/`Variant`/`Dynamic` from the `Field`-based `SingleValueDataGeneric`. `ColumnObject::compareAt` (line 2176) is fully implemented, so the WithColumn path's comparisons work.

### The crash

I confirmed the coordinator's diagnosis and verified it is the only crash site. In `AggregateFunctionSingleValueOrNull.cpp`:
- constructor sets `serialization = type->getDefaultSerialization()` (the **non-nullable** JSON serialization) and `result_type = makeNullable(type)`
- `deserialize` (lines 170-173) calls `data().read(buf, *serialization, result_type, arena)` — passing `result_type = Nullable(JSON)`

The `add`/`merge`/`serialize`/`insertResultInto` paths are all safe for JSON (they operate on real `ColumnObject`s produced by `set`). The cleanest fix is for `singleValueOrNull`'s `deserialize` to pass `value_type` (non-nullable) instead of `result_type`, keeping the column type consistent with the serialization. Note also the pre-existing `TODO` at `AggregateFunctionSingleValueOrNull.cpp:79` about `write`/`read` losing `first_value`/`is_null`, which is a separate correctness limitation.

I did not modify anything.

Both independent investigations confirm the diagnosis and that the `read` type mismatch is the *only* crash site — `add`/`merge`/`serialize`/`insertResultInto` are all safe for JSON. My fix is complete and minimal.

## Summary

**Root cause of the crash**

`singleValueOrNull` with the `JSON` type routes its value storage to `SingleValueDataGenericWithColumn` (because `canUseFieldForValueData` excludes `Object`/`Variant`/`Dynamic`, which don't round-trip through `Field`). That struct's `read` builds a column from the *type it's handed* and then deserializes into it:

```cpp
auto new_value = type->createColumn();
serialization.deserializeBinary(*new_value, buf, {});
```

The aggregate function's `deserialize` was passing `result_type`, which is `makeNullable(type)` = `Nullable(JSON)`. But `serialization` is built from the **non-nullable** `JSON` type. So `read` created a `ColumnNullable`, then handed it to `SerializationObject::deserializeBinary`, which does `assert_cast<ColumnObject &>(col)` (`SerializationObject.cpp:1231`) — a `ColumnNullable` is not a `ColumnObject`, producing the segfault. This is triggered whenever states are deserialized: on `singleValueOrNullMerge` reading an `AggregateFunction(singleValueOrNull, JSON)` column from `MergeTree`.

**The fix** (`src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionSingleValueOrNull.cpp`)

`deserialize` now passes `value_type` (the non-nullable `JSON` type, which matches `serialization`) instead of `result_type`, so `read` allocates a `ColumnObject` consistent with the serialization:

```cpp
data(place).read(buf, *serialization, value_type, arena);
```

**Why this satisfies the three requirements**
- In-memory aggregation (single value → that value; distinct values → `NULL`) is untouched and already works — `add`/`isEqualTo` use `ColumnObject::compareAt`.
- Table creation + `singleValueOrNullState` insertion already worked (the `serialize`/`write` path operates on a real `ColumnObject`).
- `singleValueOrNullMerge` no longer crashes; deserialization now builds the correct column type. The result is `NULL` per row because the pre-existing limitation (the `TODO` at line 79 — `write`/`read` don't persist the `first_value`/`is_null` flags) leaves `first_value == true` after deserialization, so `insertResultInto` returns the default (`NULL`). Fixing that flag persistence is a separate, format-breaking change and out of scope here.

The change is a one-line semantic fix using an already-available member; I did not modify anything under `tests/`.
